PHP is mainly focused on server-side scripting, so it can do anything any other CGI program can do, such as collect form data, generate dynamic page content, or send and receive cookies.

When PHP processes a file, it recognizes the opening and closing tags, <?php and ?>, to define the boundaries of PHP code execution. Content outside these tags is ignored by the PHP parser. If a file ends with PHP code, it is preferable to omit the PHP closing tag at the end of the file.

The closing tag of a PHP block at the end of a file is optional. The closing tag of a block of PHP code automatically implies a semicolon; you do not need to have a semicolon terminating the last line of a PHP block.
echo is not a function but a language construct. Its arguments are a list of expressions following the echo keyword, separated by commas, and not delimited by parentheses.
PHP supports 'C', 'C++' and Unix shell-style (Perl style) comments. Example: // This is a one-line c++ style comment ; /* multi line */ ; # This is a one-line shell-style comment.
The closing tag of a PHP block at the end of a file is optional.
Variables in PHP are represented by a dollar sign followed by the name of the variable. The variable name is case-sensitive. A valid variable name starts with a letter or underscore.
Unlike the double-quoted and heredoc syntaxes, variables and escape sequences for special characters will not be expanded when they occur in single quoted strings.
There is no int division operator in PHP. To achieve this, use the intdiv() function. 1/2 yields the float 0.5. var_dump(25/7); // float(3.5714285714286)
Determine if a variable is declared and is different than null. isset() will return false when checking a variable that has been assigned to null.

The bool type only has two values: true or false. When converting to bool, the integer 0, the floats 0.0 and -0.0, the empty string "" and the string "0", an array with zero elements, and NULL are considered false. Every other value is considered true.
There is no int division operator in PHP. To achieve this, use the intdiv() function. 1/2 yields the float 0.5.

A short array syntax exists which replaces array() with []. Example: $array2 = ["foo" => "bar", "bar" => "foo"]; The key can either be an int or a string. PHP arrays can contain integer and string keys at the same time.
The foreach construct provides an easy way to iterate over arrays and Traversable objects. foreach (iterable_expression as $value) and foreach (iterable_expression as $key => $value).

sources.section: Example of isset() with array elements
sources.excerpt: var_dump(isset($a['hello'])); // FALSE. The key 'hello' equals NULL so is considered unset. If you want to check for NULL key values then try: var_dump(array_key_exists('hello', $a)); // TRUE

The key can either be an int or a string. Additionally the following key casts will occur: Strings containing valid decimal ints will be cast to int type. PHP does not distinguish between indexed and associative arrays as separate types; both are the array type.

If you use an undefined constant, PHP assumes that you mean the name of the constant itself, just as if you called it as a string (CONSTANT vs "CONSTANT"). An error of level E_NOTICE is issued when this happens. As of PHP 8.0.0, an Error exception is thrown instead. Unquoted keys like $personne[prenom] therefore error in PHP 8 unless constant prenom exists.
isset() returns false if the variable is null. array_key_exists() returns true for a key whose value is null.

$a == $b Equal: true if $a is equal to $b after type juggling. $a === $b Identical: true if $a is equal to $b, and they are of the same type. These rules also apply to the switch statement. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if a string is compared to a number the string was converted to a number.

A match arm compares values strictly (===) instead of loosely as the switch statement does. A match expression returns a value. match arms do not fall through. If the subject expression is not handled by any match arm, an UnhandledMatchError is thrown.

Non-strict comparisons between numbers and non-numeric strings now work by casting the number to string and comparing the strings. Notably, this means that 0 == "not-a-number" is considered false now. 0 == "foo" : Before true, After false.

When converting to bool, the following values are considered false: the boolean false itself; the integer 0; the floats 0.0 and -0.0; the empty string "" and the string "0"; an array with zero elements; the unit type NULL. Every other value is considered true.
Note that switch/case does a loose comparison. It is equivalent to if ($i == 0) / elseif ($i == 1).
PHP 8.3: Active Support Until 31 Dec 2025; Security Support Until 31 Dec 2027. PHP 8.0 is end of life (not in the currently supported table). PHP 7 branches are end of life.

for loops are the most complex loops in PHP. The syntax of a for loop is: for (expr1; expr2; expr3) statement. The first expression (expr1) is evaluated (executed) once unconditionally at the beginning of the loop.

The meaning of a while statement is simple. It tells PHP to execute the nested statement(s) repeatedly, as long as the while expression evaluates to true. The value of the expression is checked each time at the beginning of the loop.

do-while loops are very similar to while loops, except the truth expression is checked at the end of each iteration instead of in the beginning. The main difference from regular while loops is that the first iteration of a do-while loop is guaranteed to run.

break ends execution of the current for, foreach, while, do-while or switch structure. break accepts an optional numeric argument which tells it how many nested enclosing structures are to be broken out of.
continue is used within looping structures to skip the rest of the current loop iteration and continue execution at the condition evaluation and then the beginning of the next iteration.
count — Counts all elements in an array or in a Countable object. Returns the number of elements in value. When used with an array, counts all elements in the array.

Functions need not be defined before they are referenced, except when a function is conditionally defined. When a function is defined in a conditional manner, its definition must be processed prior to being called.

Note that any optional parameters should be specified after any required parameters, otherwise they cannot be omitted from calls. As of PHP 8.0.0, declaring mandatory parameters after optional parameters is deprecated. Example output: Deprecated: makeyogurt(): Optional parameter $container declared before required parameter $flavour is implicitly treated as a required parameter.
If the return is omitted the value null will be returned.

Arrow functions were introduced in PHP 7.4 as a more concise syntax for anonymous functions. Arrow functions have the basic form fn (argument_list) => expr. Using variables from the parent scope is always automatic.

Type declarations can be added to function arguments, return values, and as of PHP 7.4.0 class properties. Scalar types (int, float, string, bool) were added in PHP 7.0; void in 7.1; nullable types with ? in 7.1.
PHP 8.3 security support until 31 Dec 2027; PHP 7.4 is end of life (not listed as currently supported).
Functions need not be defined before they are referenced, except when a function is conditionally defined.

To create an instance of a class, the new keyword must be used. An object will always be created unless the object has a constructor defined that throws an exception on error. $instance = new SimpleClass();

As of PHP 7.4.0, property definitions can include Type declarations, with the exception of callable. Typed properties must be initialized before accessing, otherwise an Error is thrown. Properties may be defined using a visibility modifier, optionally (except for readonly) as of PHP 7.4, followed by a type declaration.
The pseudo-variable $this is available when a method is called from within an object context. $this is a reference to the calling object.

Type declarations can be added to function arguments, return values, as of PHP 7.4.0, class properties, and as of PHP 8.3.0, class constants. They ensure that the value is of the specified type at call time, otherwise a TypeError is thrown.
Class properties may be defined as public, private, or protected. Properties declared without any explicit visibility keyword are defined as public.
Typed properties are available as of PHP 7.4.0.

The visibility of a property, a method or (as of PHP 7.1.0) a constant can be defined by prefixing the declaration with public, protected or private. Class members declared public can be accessed everywhere. Members declared protected can be accessed only within the class itself and by inheriting and parent classes. Members declared as private may only be accessed by the class that defines the member.

As of PHP 8.0.0, constructor parameters may also be promoted to correspond to an object property. It is very common for constructor parameters to be assigned to a property. Promotion combines declaration and assignment.
Declaring class properties or methods as static makes them accessible without needing an instantiation of the class. These can also be accessed statically within an instantiated class object.
It is possible to define constants on a per-class basis. The default visibility of class constants is public.
PASSWORD_DEFAULT - Use the bcrypt algorithm (default as of PHP 5.5.0). Note that this constant is designed to change over time as new and stronger algorithms are added to PHP.

A file containing a namespace must declare the namespace at the top of the file before any other code - with one exception: the declare keyword. The only code construct allowed before a namespace declaration is the declare statement.

Aliasing is accomplished with the use operator. Example: use My\Full\Classname as Another; use ArrayObject; // importing a global class. PHP can alias/import constants, functions, classes, interfaces, traits, enums and namespaces.
Namespaces are a way of encapsulating items to avoid name collisions. PHP Namespaces provide a way in which to group related classes, interfaces, functions and constants.

To obtain the fully qualified name of a class ClassName use ClassName::class. Example in namespace NS: echo ClassName::class; output: NS\ClassName (no leading backslash). As of PHP 8.0.0, ::class may also be used on objects; its effect is the same as calling get_class() on the object.
Classes, functions and constants being imported from the same namespace can now be grouped together in a single use statement. use some\namespace\{ClassA, ClassB, ClassC as C};

Many developers writing object-oriented applications create one PHP source file per class definition. The spl_autoload_register() function registers any number of autoloaders, enabling classes and interfaces to be automatically loaded if they are currently not defined. Any class-like construct may be autoloaded the same way. That includes classes, interfaces, traits, and enumerations.
A file containing a namespace must declare the namespace at the top of the file before any other code - with one exception: the declare keyword.
PHP attributes provide structured, machine-readable metadata for classes, methods, functions, parameters, properties, and constants. They can be inspected at runtime via the Reflection API.

An attribute declaration starts with #[ and ends with ]. Inside, one or more attributes can be listed, separated by commas. Arguments to the attribute are optional and enclosed in parentheses (). Both positional and named argument syntax are supported.

public function __construct(string|array|null $path = null, ?string $name = null, array $requirements = [], array $options = [], array $defaults = [], ?string $host = null, array|string $methods = [], ...). The third positional parameter is $requirements, not $methods.

decimal: Maps and converts numeric data with fixed-point precision. Values retrieved from the database are always converted to PHP's string type or null if no data is present. For compatibility reasons this type is not converted to a double as PHP can only preserve the precision to a certain degree.

sources.excerpt: As of version 4, the DBAL uses identity columns to implement the autoincrement behavior on PostgreSQL instead of SERIAL* column types.

Object interfaces allow you to create code which specifies which methods and properties a class must implement, without having to define how these methods or properties are implemented. All methods declared in an interface must be public. It's possible for interfaces to have constants. As of PHP 8.4.0, interfaces may also declare properties.

Classes defined as abstract cannot be instantiated, and any class that contains at least one abstract method or property must also be abstract. Methods defined as abstract simply declare the method's signature; they cannot define the implementation. When inheriting from an abstract class, all methods marked abstract in the parent's class declaration must be defined by the child class.
public function eraseCredentials(): void; @deprecated since Symfony 7.3, erase credentials using the "__serialize()" method instead. getRoles(): array and getUserIdentifier(): string remain required.

In Symfony 7.3, this method has been deprecated. To ease the upgrade path, Symfony 7.3 allows you to add the #[\Deprecated] attribute to your eraseCredentials() method. When present, Symfony will stop calling the method automatically.

Traits are a mechanism for code reuse in single inheritance languages such as PHP. A Trait is similar to a class, but only intended to group functionality. It is not possible to instantiate a Trait on its own. To resolve naming conflicts between Traits used in the same class, the insteadof operator needs to be used. The as operator can be used to add an alias.

If two Traits insert a method with the same name, a fatal error is produced, if the conflict is not explicitly resolved. To resolve naming conflicts, the insteadof operator needs to be used to choose exactly one of the conflicting methods. The as operator can be used to add an alias to one of the methods.

sources.section: PHP RFC: Namespaced names as a single token (implemented PHP 8.0)
sources.excerpt: PHP currently treats namespaced names like Foo\Bar as a sequence of identifiers and namespace separator tokens. This RFC proposes to treat namespaced names as a single token, and as such allow reserved keywords to appear inside them. Individual namespace segments may contain reserved keywords. Target Version: PHP 8.0. Status: Implemented. namespace iter\fn; is legal.

As of PHP 7.1.0, a catch block may specify multiple exceptions using the pipe (|) character. As of PHP 8.0.0, the variable name for a caught exception is optional. Code within the finally block will always be executed after the try and catch blocks, regardless of whether an exception has been thrown. The set_exception_handler() function can set a function that will be called if no other catch block is invoked.
Multiple exceptions per catch block may now be specified using the pipe character (|). This is useful for when different exceptions from different class hierarchies are handled the same.

PHP 7 changes how most errors are reported by PHP. Most errors are now reported by throwing Error exceptions. As the Error hierarchy does not inherit from Exception, catch (Exception $e) blocks will find that these Errors are not caught. Throwable > Error (TypeError, DivisionByZeroError, ...) and Exception.

An interface declaration is another way to name an object type. TypeScript is only concerned with the structure of the value we passed - it only cares that it has the expected properties. Being concerned only with the structure and capabilities of types is why we call TypeScript a structurally typed type system.

Much of the time, we'll find ourselves dealing with objects that might have a property set. In those cases, we can mark those properties as optional by adding a question mark (?) to the end of their names. Properties can also be marked as readonly for TypeScript.

A union type is a type formed from two or more other types, representing values that may be any one of those types. TypeScript will only allow an operation if it is valid for every member of the union.
When every type in a union contains a common property with literal types, TypeScript considers that to be a discriminated union, and can narrow out the members of the union.
The unknown type represents any value. This is similar to the any type, but is safer because it's not legal to do anything with an unknown value.
In TypeScript, we can specify a function that can be called in different ways by writing overload signatures. Always prefer parameters with union types instead of overloads when possible.

TypeScript offers special syntax for turning a constructor parameter into a class property with the same name and value. These are called parameter properties and are created by prefixing a constructor argument with one of the visibility modifiers public, private, protected, or readonly.

The default visibility of class members is public. protected members are only visible to subclasses of the class they're declared in. private is like protected, but doesn't allow access to the member even from subclasses.

In modern TypeScript, you may not need an enum when an object with as const could suffice. The biggest argument in favour of this format over TypeScript's enum is that it keeps your codebase aligned with the state of JavaScript.

Enums are a feature added to JavaScript by TypeScript which allows for describing a value which could be one of a set of possible named constants. Because of this, it's a feature which you should know exists, but maybe hold off on using unless you are sure.

TShark's native capture file format is pcapng. -f capture filter, -Y display filter. Display filters are currently not supported when capturing and saving. -s 0 specifies a snapshot length of 262144 (default). -p Don't put the interface into promiscuous mode. -D print interfaces and exit. -G fields[,prefix] dumps the registration database. -z statistics are calculated independently of the main display filter. filesize:value kB; example -b filesize:1000 -b files:5 = five files of size one megabyte each. Positional filter: capture filter if live, display filter if -r.

sources.title: Nixon ends gold convertibility
sources.excerpt: On the evening of August 15, 1971, Nixon addressed the nation on a new economic policy. The first order was for the gold window to be closed. Foreign governments could no longer exchange their dollars for gold; in effect, the international monetary system turned into a fiat one.

sources.section: FIPS 203 Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (13 Aug 2024)
sources.excerpt: This standard specifies a key-encapsulation mechanism called ML-KEM. This standard specifies three parameter sets for ML-KEM. In order of increasing security strength and decreasing performance, these are ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. Related NIST Publications: FIPS 204, FIPS 205.
